labels.DOMAIN_REACHABILITY_UNKNOWN: whether a real plan can contain this pattern (how many same-zone pickups at what spacing) is NOT settled here (N-12)
labels.EXECUTOR_REPRODUCED: the real code, through the public API, produces the same state (N-02, N-03)
labels.MATHEMATICAL_COUNTEREXAMPLE: the band-invariant claim is false in exact arithmetic (N-01, N-04)

rows.name: N-01 the twice-opened zone-1 value exceeds the claimed bound tau+delta (MATHEMATICAL_COUNTEREXAMPLE)
N-02 the EXECUTOR reproduces it through the PUBLIC api (EXECUTOR_REPRODUCED)
N-03 the INTERNAL executor pair agrees with the public api and with Path-M
N-04 nine consecutive doors in one zone keep accumulating (no self-limiting) (MATHEMATICAL_COUNTEREXAMPLE + EXECUTOR_REPRODUCED)
N-05 the counterexample satisfies EVERY declared premise D1-D6, so the domain restriction does not exclude it

detail.checked: one door per zone from tau

rows.name: N-06 L1 (floor) holds: after any segment the value is >= tau
N-07 L2 as stated is TRUE and in the direction Phi(T0) >= Phi(tau) for T0 >= tau -- which is the opposite of the step Theorem B used
N-08 L3 holds: under the drift condition, Phi is non-increasing in t from T0 = tau

detail.root_cause: the drift condition bounds the SLOPE, not the RETURN TIME; returning to tau takes up to delta/margin hours, which a short segment does not provide
detail.theorem_A: per-segment extremes need only L3 and stay valid
detail.theorem_B: REFUTED by N-01/N-02/N-04: a short segment leaves Phi above tau, so the next door stacks on top of it

rows.name: N-09 Theorem A (per-segment, no door) survives audit; Theorem B (band invariant for ANY segment sequence) does NOT
N-10 the dt <= _EPS branch keeps the pre-door value (no cooling, no clamp) and the door then adds delta -- so the branch does NOT restore the band

detail.reading: the nine-door states are still inside the hard bounds, so no hard-bound VIOLATION is demonstrated here; what is refuted is the SUFFICIENCY ARGUMENT, because the state leaves the band it was proved to stay in. A hard-bound violation needs enough doors to be REACHED, which is a reachability question (N-13).

rows.name: N-11 B2 NECESSITY keeps its basis (the band endpoints are attainable), but B2 SUFFICIENCY as stated is NOT established: the invariant it relies on is refuted

detail.label: DOMAIN_REACHABILITY_UNKNOWN: whether a real plan can contain that many same-zone pickups with such short segments is NOT settled by this audit

rows.name: N-12 accumulation has no self-limit: with dt = 0.01 h the zone-1 value would reach the hard upper bound after a finite number of doors

detail.conclusion: a single-segment sample set is structurally incapable of validating a cross-segment invariant

rows.name: N-13 the earlier 4000-sample check could not detect this by construction: it sampled ONE segment from T0 and compared paths, so no cross-segment composition was ever exercised

detail.measured: worst case exceeds tau+delta as soon as segments are shorter than the return time; N-01 gives tau+delta+0.0709 for a two-door pattern
detail.spec_claim: T-Q2-5a is covered by Theorem B, worst case exactly tau+delta

rows.name: N-14 T-Q2-5a (consecutive doors accumulating warming) IS a genuine counterexample to Theorem B, so the specification s claim that Theorem B covers it is inverted
